ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two oblique straight lines a and b, intersected by the same transverse oblique line c. The left intersection point is R, and the right intersection point is P; above R on line a is labeled M, and to the right of R on line c it leads to Q. Therefore ∠MRQ is the angle at R formed by RM and RQ, labeled in the figure as (5x+7)°. At P, between the two oblique lines and on the other side of line c, it is labeled (7x−21)°. Reasoning: To make a ∥ b, these two angles should be alternate interior angles and equal, so 5x+7 = 7x−21. Solving gives 28 = 2x, therefore x = 14. Substituting into m∠MRQ = 5x+7 gives 5(14)+7 = 70+7 = 77°.
